Xeon8375C.registration: MurmurHash2a                   32                      MurmurHash v2a, 32-bit version using variant mixing

M2Pro.registration: MurmurHash2a                   32                      MurmurHash v2a, 32-bit version using variant mixing

Xeon8375C.registration: MurmurHash3-128               128                      MurmurHash v3, 128-bit version using 64-bit variables

M2Pro.registration: MurmurHash3-128               128                      MurmurHash v3, 128-bit version using 64-bit variables

hashes.XXH3-64: same-binary control; published value in speeds.json
hashes.MurmurHash3-128: same-binary control; published value in speeds.json

protocol.command: SMHasher3 NAME --test=Speed (unmodified harness, no overrides); SMHasher3 NAME --test=Sanity once per hash and host
protocol.bulk: Average of alignments 0..7 at fixed 262144 bytes (SMHasher3 Average line)
protocol.small: Average of the 31 separately measured 1..31-byte costs
protocol.xeon: two complete passes; higher fixed-size bulk (ties: higher GiB/s, then earlier) and lower small average (ties: earlier) selected independently
protocol.m2: three complete passes; median of bulk and median of small, independently; any run deviating more than 15 percent from its median is flagged, never dropped
protocol.order: Sanity for all seven names, then pass 1 over all seven names, then pass 2 (and pass 3 on the M2); one SMHasher3 process at a time

affinity.Xeon8375C: nice -n 10 taskset -c 16-23 (the post's range; the host has CPUs 0-95 only); per-CPU busy samples of 16-23 before and after each run

load_gate.Xeon8375C: no other SMHasher3 process and load1 < 80 (shared host; other users' unpinned jobs)
load_gate.M2Pro: no other SMHasher3 process and load1 < 4.5; 60 s polls

Xeon8375C.base: the post's Xeon SMHasher3 Release build (build-release-20260917), the same binary as the XXH3-64 and MurmurHash3-128 rows of speeds.json

M2Pro.base: the public timing reproduction's arm64 build (pin 3de870c7 + patch series incl. the arm64 family.cmake fix), the same base as speeds_polyxor.json. The post's M2 binary (m2-rerun/build-fixed, sha256 fb2f75fb...) no longer exists on disk; the controls here are same-binary controls against the published speeds.json values of that other binary.

units.gib_s: printed GiB/s assumes 3.5 GHz on both hosts; a conversion of B/cycle
